quizzes.title: Early History of Caste-Based Reservation: MCQ
quizzes.passage:
The idea of caste-based reservation in India was first proposed in 1882, long before the present Constitution came into force. During British rule, elements of reservation took the form of separate electorates, a system in which members of a particular community chose their own representatives. This arrangement was not confined to a single group. Over time, the British applied separate electorates to several categories of people, and the arrangements were revised more than once.

After independence, the question of reservation was taken up within the new constitutional framework. The Constitution's guarantees of equality shaped how any special treatment could be provided, and courts were asked to examine whether particular measures were valid under them. Governments therefore had to fit their policies within these limits, and the judiciary had a decisive role in deciding where the limits lay.

Commissions were also set up to study the condition of backward classes, and their findings informed policy. Courts, in turn, ruled on reservation policies in several important cases, and those rulings set out conditions and ceilings that governments must observe when they design reservation schemes. The result is a system in which political choices and legal review have shaped each other over the decades.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. IR Coelho case (2007)   ->   A. First Backward Class Commission (national level)
II. Janhit Abhiyan case (2022)   ->   B. Laws placed in the 9th Schedule after 24 April 1973 subject to judicial review
III. Kalelkar Commission (1953)   ->   C. Abandoned separate electorates for Depressed Classes
IV. Poona Pact   ->   D. Upheld the 103rd Amendment (EWS reservation)
questions.explanation: IR Coelho matches the 9th Schedule ruling, Janhit matches upholding the 103rd Amendment, Kalelkar matches the first Backward Class Commission, and Poona Pact matches abandoning separate electorates.

questions.q: Who first proposed caste-based reservation in 1882?
options: B.G. Tilak and Gopal Krishna Gokhale
questions.explanation: The booklet names William Hunter and Jyotirao Phule as the proponents of caste-based reservation in 1882.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Kalelkar Commission was set up in 1953.
Reason (R): The Kalelkar Commission identified only Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: A is true, but R is false because the Kalelkar Commission identified backward classes other than SCs and STs.

questions.q: Which groups did the Government of India Act of 1935 extend separate electorates to?
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act of 1935 extended separate electorates to the Depressed Classes, Women and Labour.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the MR Balaji case (1963):
I. The case was against the State of Mysore.
II. The Court ordered the government to keep reservation at 50 per cent.
III. The judgement was delivered in 1979.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while the Balaji judgement was delivered in 1963, not 1979.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. Separate electorates were introduced under the Government of India Act of 1909.
II. The Mandal Commission was set up in 1953.
III. The MacDonald/Communal Award of 1932 provided separate electorates for Depressed Classes.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while the Mandal Commission was set up in 1979, not 1953.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment added Article 15(4) to legalise caste-based reservation?
questions.explanation: The 1st Constitutional Amendment of 1951 added Article 15(4).

quizzes.title: Later Judgements and EWS Reservation: MCQ
quizzes.passage:
Judgements after the early 1990s have refined how reservation works. Courts have considered whether the State must provide reservation in promotions, how laws placed in the Ninth Schedule are treated, and which members of a reserved group should be excluded from its benefits. Such rulings have set conditions that governments must meet before they can act.

The Constitution has also been amended to address economically weaker sections. One amendment introduced a quota for these groups, and the Supreme Court later examined it. The same route of constitutional change was used for women. Another amendment set aside a share of seats in Parliament and State Legislatures for women, and these seats may be allotted by rotation among constituencies. The reservation is not permanent, and the provision was designed to lapse after a fixed period.

Economic criteria have therefore entered the reservation framework alongside social criteria. The basic principle of reserving seats or posts for disadvantaged groups remains, but the basis on which groups are identified has widened. Each new measure must still be tested against the Constitution's guarantees, and the courts examine whether it meets the required conditions. This is why each change in the rules is closely examined in the courts and by the government that proposes it.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment provided 10 per cent reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS)?
questions.explanation: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment of 2019 provided 10 per cent reservation for EWS.

questions.q: What share of seats did the 106th Amendment Act reserve for women in Parliament and State Legislatures?
questions.explanation: The 106th Amendment Act reserves one-third of seats for women in Parliament and State Legislatures.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Under the Jarnail Singh judgement (2018), the State must collect quantifiable data on SC/ST backwardness before giving reservation in promotions.
Reason (R): The Nagaraj case (2006) laid down that a State must collect quantifiable data on backwardness before providing reservation in promotions.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: A is false because Jarnail Singh held that quantifiable data is not required, while R is true for the Nagaraj case.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Janhit Abhiyan case (2022)   ->   B. Report submitted in July 2010
II. Commission for Economically Backward Classes   ->   C. Reservation in promotions does not need quantifiable data
III. 102nd Constitutional Amendment (2018)   ->   D. Gave constitutional status to the NCBC
IV. Jarnail Singh case (2018)   ->   A. Upheld the 103rd Amendment
questions.explanation: Janhit upheld the 103rd Amendment, the EWS commission reported in July 2010, the 102nd Amendment gave NCBC constitutional status, and Jarnail Singh said no quantifiable data is needed.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Nagaraj case (2006) and the Jarnail Singh case (2018):
I. A State must show that it does not compromise on efficiency of administration.
II. A State must prove inadequate representation of the class in public employment.
III. The Jarnail Singh case requires quantifiable data for reservation in promotions for SCs and STs.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are Nagaraj conditions, while Jarnail Singh did not require quantifiable data, so III is incorrect.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The Commission for Economically Backward Classes was constituted in 2005.
II. The 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act was passed in 2018.
III. The Janhit Abhiyan judgement was delivered in 2018.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while the Janhit Abhiyan judgement was delivered in 2022, not 2018.

questions.q: For how many years will the reservation of seats for women under the 106th Amendment remain in effect?
questions.explanation: The reservation ceases to exist after 15 years from the date of implementation.

quizzes.title: National Commission for Backward Classes: MCQ
quizzes.passage:
A permanent body for backward classes was first envisaged in a 1992 judgement on reservation. The judgement directed that a permanent statutory body should be set up to examine complaints of over-inclusion and under-inclusion in the list of backward classes, so that benefits reach those who need them. Errors in either direction, whether a community is wrongly included or wrongly left out, were what the direction aimed to address. The aim was to keep the list accurate so that the reservation system works as intended.

The second Backward Classes Commission is one example of the inquiries that preceded this idea. It was appointed to study the conditions of socially and educationally backward classes and to suggest measures for their advancement, and its work dealt with the same underlying question of who needs support.

The national body that was eventually created came through an Act of Parliament. Its work concerns the welfare of backward classes and the examination of matters that affect them. Because it operates within the wider framework of reservation, its findings bear on the economic criteria that decide who is excluded from benefits, and on how reservation is shared among groups. Its role is therefore closely tied to the working of reservation as a whole.

questions.q: In which year was the National Commission for Backward Classes set up by an Act of Parliament?
questions.explanation: The NCBC was set up in 1993 by an Act of Parliament.

questions.q: Under which Article of the Constitution was constitutional status given to the NCBC?
questions.explanation: Article 338B gave the NCBC constitutional status and increased the scope of its functions.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The conditions of service and tenure of the NCBC's members are determined by the President.
Reason (R): The NCBC was set up in 1993.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the year of setting up does not explain the President's power over service and tenure.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Article 338B   ->   B. Members appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal
II. Article 342A   ->   D. Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and three other members
III. Composition of the NCBC   ->   C. Gave constitutional status and wider functions to the NCBC
IV. Warrant under hand and seal   ->   A. Empowers the President to specify backward classes in States and UTs
questions.explanation: Article 338B gives constitutional status, Article 342A empowers the President to specify backward classes, the NCBC has a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and three members, and members are appointed by warrant.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Backward Classes:
I. The NCBC can recommend the income level that excludes the creamy layer from reservation benefits.
II. The NCBC members are appointed by the Prime Minister.
III. The NCBC can investigate complaints relating to backward classes.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while members are appointed by the President, not the Prime Minister.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The NCBC's members are appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.
II. The NCBC was set up by an Act of Parliament in 1963.
III. The NCBC was set up by the original Constitution in 1950.
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since the NCBC was set up by an Act of Parliament in 1993, not 1963 or by the original Constitution.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act of 2018 gave the NCBC constitutional status?
questions.explanation: The 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 2018 gave the NCBC constitutional status.
